comparisons.finding: Strongest reader. Dedicated titles identify the content; full-width paragraphs and a clear bottom return support long reading. At 200%, the wrapped heading adds overhead but answers remain immediately accessible.
The selector is legible, but no selected content appears in either reason or answers captures at either size. The supplied pictures leave the core reading task unanswered: overall capped at 4.

Clear disclosure indicators and readable paragraphs. However, the answers capture retains the expanded reason above answers, contrary to the stated single-open behavior. At 200%, the requested answers are entirely below the viewport; section switching carries substantial scroll cost.

Best immediate connection between forecast and evaluation. Radio selection, status and Save form a coherent sequence. At 200%, Save requires scrolling; the saved capture leaves it below the viewport. Saved feedback is explicit, but the unchanged Save label weakens completion.

Strongest across both sizes: all choices, adjacent status and Save fit at 200%. The overview establishes the forecast, although collapsing it during evaluation adds recall burden. Saved wording communicates completion, but Save remains visually unchanged.

Fixed Save stays prominent and the exact forecast remains visible. At 200%, the footer cuts across the options area; the saved message increases its height until only the first choice is visible. Reachability of the remaining choices within the claimed scrollable sheet is not demonstrated.

Strongest coherent Home. The orb retains prominence while unavailable status, consumed attempt and tomorrow are plainly stated. The descriptive disclosure preserves context; the complete policy remains readable at 200%, with added scrolling.

At 200%, the split status/Details row squeezes the status into five short lines. Details is less descriptive than A's disclosure. The policy sheet is readable with a prominent Done button, but the isolated orb pedestal distracts from its content.

Full-width status wraps better than B and preserves the hero. However, 'Unavailable · try tomorrow ›' ambiguously combines status, instruction and navigation. The used-attempt summary starts below the initial 200% viewport. The policy sheet retains the distracting detached pedestal.

reason: A gives reading details a focused destination and Home a clear explanation in context. B gives check-in the strongest enlarged-text composition, keeping choices, feedback and Save together. Scores cover visible screen and component composition; none establishes the requested 9/9 threshold.
limitations: Screenshot-only provisional assessment. Feedback scores concern visible selection, disclosure and status changes, not verified interaction semantics or persistence.
Evidence B's described selected content is absent from the supplied images; evidence C's answers state visibly retains the expanded reason.
No proof of keyboard operation, focus restoration, screen-reader announcements, target hit areas, measured contrast, reduced motion or native behavior.
Check-in C's lower-choice reachability at 200% is unestablished; the pictures show footer occlusion but cannot establish whether scrolling resolves it.
